summary: This is a clipped pandas 2.2.2 API reference page for Series.dt.tz_localize, which localizes tz-naive datetime Series/Index objects to tz-aware ones (or removes timezone info by passing tz=None) without changing the underlying time. It documents the parameters tz, ambiguous and nonexistent, the return and error behavior (TypeError when already tz-aware and tz is not None), and gives examples using US/Eastern, CET and Europe/Warsaw, including DST handling. Navigation menus, repeated site headers and footer boilerplate were ignored.
one_line: pandas 2.2.2 API reference page describing Series.dt.tz_localize for converting tz-naive datetimes to tz-aware ones and handling DST ambiguity.
key_facts: The pandas method Series.dt.tz_localize localizes tz-naive Datetime Array/Index to tz-aware Datetime Array/Index without moving the time to another time zone.
Passing tz=None to tz_localize removes time zone information while preserving local time.
The ambiguous parameter defaults to 'raise' and accepts 'infer', 'NaT', or a bool array, where True signifies a DST time.
The nonexistent parameter defaults to 'raise' and accepts 'shift_forward', 'shift_backward', 'NaT', or a timedelta object.
The method raises a TypeError if the Datetime Array/Index is tz-aware and tz is not None.
The documented page is for pandas version 2.2.2, copyright 2024.
In the example, tz_naive = pd.date_range('2018-03-01 09:00', periods=3) localized to US/Eastern gives times such as '2018-03-01 09:00:00-05:00'.
In Central European Time (UTC+01), local time 02:30:00 on the DST fall-back day occurs both at 00:30:00 UTC and at 01:30:00 UTC.
Using ambiguous='infer' on the CET example series assigns +02:00 to the first 02:00 and +01:00 to the second 02:00 on 2018-10-28.
Using nonexistent='shift_forward' on Europe/Warsaw shifts 2015-03-29 02:30:00 to 03:00:00+02:00.
Using nonexistent='shift_backward' on Europe/Warsaw shifts 2015-03-29 02:30:00 to 01:59:59.999999999+01:00.
Using nonexistent=pd.Timedelta('1h') on Europe/Warsaw shifts 2015-03-29 02:30:00 to 03:30:00+02:00.
The See also section points to DatetimeIndex.tz_convert, which converts tz-aware DatetimeIndex from one time zone to another.
The page was built with Sphinx 7.2.6 and the PyData Sphinx Theme 0.14.4.
